shelfmark: Groninger Archieven, 696 Familie van Ewsum, inv. nr. 595
how: All 199 scans as screenshots of the archieven.nl viewer (anl_view.js), on contact sheets: scans 1-18 and 55-150 at 330 px an opening, 19-54 at 220 px, 151-199 at 250-330 px; scans 1, 157, 192, 193, 194 enlarged. A scan is one opening (two pages).

cipher_leaves.what: The cipher opening, in its place near the end of the register. Left page: two key lines (clear letters over symbols), a three-line note in clear Dutch, about 20 lines of symbol cipher. Right page: 9 cipher lines, a 3-word cipher line, then the clear Latin caption 'ad perforandum caput gallinae'. No decipherment on the opening.
The same opening as scan 193, put first in the scan order (same layout and text); not a second cipher leaf.

not_cipher.note: the cipher of scan 193 shows through the paper; the writing on these openings is clear. Scan 192 right page carries clear household recipes (the first headed, as read, 'Eine goet rotten kruyt tho maken'), which suggests the cipher notes are recipes too.
loose dark slips lying in the book are pieces of blotting or packing paper with ink spots, not writing
binding waste from a medieval Latin manuscript and loose clear notes
rent entries in clear cursive under place headings, and many blank openings

result: One cipher opening only (scan 193 = scan 1), about 30 lines, with its key on the same page. The 158 scans the first pass had not seen add no cipher.
limits: Scans 19-54 were read at 220 px an opening: enough to tell the upright separate cipher symbols from cursive, not enough to rule out a single cipher word inside a clear entry.
